content: 1. MONUROL should not be used in more than a single dose to treat one episode of acute cystitis. Administering repeated daily doses does not improve clinical outcomes or microbiological eradication rates compared to a single dose, but it does increase the likelihood of adverse events. Urine samples for culture and susceptibility testing should be collected both before and after completing therapy. 2. Patients should be informed that MONUROL can be taken with or without food. They should expect symptom improvement within two to three days after taking MONUROL. If symptoms do not improve, they should contact their healthcare provider. 3. Patients should be made aware that diarrhea is a common side effect of antibiotics and usually resolves after discontinuing the antibiotic. However, if they develop watery or bloody stools, with or without stomach cramps and fever, even up to two months after completing the antibiotic course, they should contact their physician immediately. 4. When MONUROL is coadministered with metoclopramide, a drug that increases gastrointestinal motility, the serum concentration and urinary excretion of fosfomycin are reduced. Other drugs that enhance gastrointestinal motility may have similar effects. Cimetidine, however, does not alter the pharmacokinetics of fosfomycin when used with MONUROL. 5. Long-term carcinogenicity studies in animals have not been conducted because MONUROL is intended for single-dose treatment in humans. MONUROL has not shown mutagenic or genotoxic effects in various in vitro and in vivo tests, including the Ames bacterial reversion test, cultured human lymphocytes, Chinese hamster V79 cells, and the mouse micronucleus assay. It also did not impair fertility or reproductive performance in male and female rats. 6. MONUROL is classified as Pregnancy Category B. Fosfomycin crosses the placental barrier when administered intramuscularly as the sodium salt at a dose of 1 gram in pregnant women. In animal studies, MONUROL did not cause teratogenic effects in pregnant rats at doses up to 1000 mg/kg/day, which is significantly higher than the human dose. However, in pregnant rabbits, fetotoxicities were observed at maternally toxic doses, likely due to the rabbit's sensitivity to changes in intestinal microflora caused by the antibiotic. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women, so MONUROL should only be used during pregnancy if clearly necessary. 7. It is unknown whether fosfomycin tromethamine is excreted in human breast milk. Since many drugs are excreted in breast milk and there is potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, a decision should be made to either discontinue nursing or avoid administering the drug, considering the drug's importance to the mother. 8. The safety and effectiveness of MONUROL in children aged 12 years and under have not been established in adequate and well-controlled studies. 9. Clinical studies of MONUROL did not include enough participants aged 65 and older to determine whether their responses differ from those of younger patients. However, other clinical experiences have not identified significant differences in responses between elderly and younger patients. In general, dosing for elderly patients should be cautious, typically starting at the lower end of the dosing range, due to the higher likelihood of decreased hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, as well as the presence of other diseases or concurrent drug therapies.
